reviews.comment:
Highly Efficient and engaging professor. 
Always looked forward to the classes, even though they were online

Faron gets a lot of hate here but if you want to learn SAS, he's your guy. Homework can be a bit difficult to decipher and tests are multiple choice with multiple right answers which is not always the best way to test programming knowledge.
The class is poorly delivered and too much homework for the students who have lab work to do
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is 1/3rd R while the other 2/3rds is SAS. The emphasis on SAS, which is outdated and rigid unlike R is too much imo. There is homework every week and each homework is a coding project on its own with and takes a ton of work to complete. The exams are multiple choice with trick questions which isn't the best way to assess coding skills

He isn't the best professor I have ever had, but I have certainly had worse as TAMU. He is TERRIBLE at teaching R, but decent at SAS. Not a nice guy, but as an online only class you really don't have to interact with him. His tests are bad, but they are open note so you can pass this class with a B pretty easily. I would give him a C as a teacher

Yes, he has multi-choice programming tests where he often has 6 or seven choices with no partial credit. This guy is obnoxious and unapologetically so. I had to take this course as a distance master' student and I did get a little bit of local Texas flavor with his talk about hog-hunting and his local pastor. He's horrible and he's proud to be so.

From what I gathered, Prof K views his students as his adversaries and doesn't care to hide it. Lectures are filled with his sighs/irritation directed towards questions - it doesn't encourage people to participate. Tests are not meant to assess competence - they seemingly aim to "trick" you so that Prof K can pat himself on the back afterwards

Base R is compared to full-feature SAS so very biased (No Rstudio/Markdown) - SAS is expensive, obsolete, and skill not transferable (macro language). Learn R/Python instead esp. for Data Science (+3 yrs exp senior DS here). Tests focused on rote memory/tricks. Sift through commas/semicolons for syntax errors instead of solving problems, awful.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The topics covered really are not difficult. The problem is his homework instructions are literally margin-to-margin BLOCKS of text with garbage grammar. They're not difficult because of the material; they're difficult because he can't write, and it's tough to understand what he's asking for. And he doesn't even have a language barrier excuse.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are super tricky and hard (select all that apply). A lot of students were kicked out during the semester due to using code from the internet. He never bumps up grades. If you got 89.9, you will get a B. Mr. Kincheloe does not respect students. I wouldnt take his class ever again. He is one of the worst instructors Ive ever seen.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but stuck in the late 90's to 00's as a lot of academic types are often a decade behind everyone else. Class way too heavily focused on SAS to the point of it being laughable. Will use your final exam to replace a test grade, but wont let the final exam replace a homework grade. Odd logic. Should have covered more R and less SAS.

Faron is not the best lecturer and his style is a bit outdated. R is used more in the industry than SAS. Hard to listen to boring lectures about something you won't really use (SAS). He doesn't really understand R programming either. Test are about tricking you rather than programming concepts.

Good lecturer: concise, comprehensive, answers questions, a few jokes here & there. Weekly homework is reasonable in length and time--not easy, but not crazy either. However, the tests can throw you for a loop if you aren't used to the format (multiple choice answers where more than one choice can be selected, but no partial credit).
He's great, easy lecturer to listen too and kinda funny

The professor was one of the horrible I've ever had.  He teaches basics from the institutes but his test gives very specific and the multiple answers doesn't give us a great way to learn. He doesn't give any partial credit for the work. He wants us to have the perfect for the homework and test. He's teaching ABC but wants us to apply with the sente

If you never programmed before, this class might be a little frustrating at times, but just dont wait last minute to do homework and youll be fine.   Test can be very tricky, but if you look over your homework and look over all the power points and really know the application of R and SAS youll do fine.

I felt like this course was relatively easy considering it is a graduate course. The homeworks can take time but I could finish them in a day or two compared to several days for other courses. If you get stuck the discussion board is very helpful and Prof K even emailed me to help with my code once. The tests require that you know the codes well.

In the first lecture he heavily emphasized how we weren't to e-mail him with questions and hasn't shown much willingness to help students at all. I am taking this class via distance education and I cannot go to office hours so I don't know how helpful he would be there but I can say there isn't much recourse for a distance student who needs help.

He starts class on a sour note with comments about no begging & no whining. He doesn't like R which is half the class material. The SAS portion is straight from SAS Institute (same books&slides). Exams are multiple choice & multiple answer, covering nitpicky details instead of good programming skills.

Thankfully, I knew R before this class. I will forgive the incomplete understanding of R as a result of taking STAT604 - it's a short semester. However,  his lectures lead to an incorrect understanding of R. His instructions are unclear and he  doesn't seem willing to specify more clearly or help. Also, WHO GIVES A MULTIPLE CHOICE PROGRAMMING TEST?

Not very clear in assignments. Each assignment is long and demands too much from students. I was taking this class to facilitate statistical analysis component of my research (I am not a statistic major), but his useless assignments were more geared towards making documents pretty. No statistics involved in the class at all.

Watch the lectures. Seriously. Do not skip this step. If you watch the lectures and take notes, the assignments are relatively easy. He is a funny guy, and the lectures are very well tailored to the weekly assignments. Accept imperfection on tests; they are reasonable, but there will be some questions that you are uncertain of no matter what.

weekly home works which each one is like a project by itself; if you do good on these, there is still no guarantee for a passing B grade considering difficulty with his exams;  no respect for student class, in his syllabus, referred to students as beggers; this mindset was obvious in his rules for the class.
